_comment: HPC Assistant local-mode configuration. Rendered into a project directory by `hpc-assistant-init --local`. This file is the policy boundary: every remote path the assistant touches is validated against remote.project_root, and every bound it honours is declared under limits. Edit it by hand as your project needs change. It holds no credentials — authentication is your ssh-agent and your ~/.ssh/config.
_comment_tool_approval: This file cannot prompt you. Per-call approval of hpc-mcp tools is the agent harness: OpenCode's local-mode overlay sets permission.hpc_* to ask in opencode.json; Claude Code gets permissions.ask mcp__hpc__* in .claude/settings.json. The overlay also denies edits of this file, opencode.json, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md.

remote._comment: host must be an alias defined in ~/.ssh/config, not a user@hostname. That is what keeps ProxyJump, MFA, certificates and ControlMaster under your control instead of the assistant's, and it is why no credential ever becomes a tool argument. project_root must be a concrete path: shell variables such as $USER and ~ are not expanded.
remote._comment_readable_paths: Directories outside project_root the assistant may READ. Sites keep shared software outside any one project, and without this the assistant cannot use it: a job that runs `singularity exec` on a site image needs that image's directory listed here. Reads only — writes stay inside project_root, so this does not widen what the assistant can damage. Both LUMI container collections are listed: /appl/local/containers holds the general images (PyTorch, JAX), and /appl/local/laifs/containers holds the LUMI AI Factory multitorch stack that the slurm skill's examples reference.

slurm._comment: default_partition has no built-in value: names like small-g are local to one cluster. extra_directives are rendered as additional #SBATCH lines (for example --gres=gpu:a100:1, --mem=32G, --cpus-per-task=8, --qos=debug). Sites that do not use --gpus-per-node should set default_gpus_per_node to 0 and put GPU syntax here.

_comment_login_commands: Site-specific CLI tools allowed on the login node in addition to the generic Unix and Slurm set. Replace these when you are not on LUMI.
_comment_env_probes: Environment variables site_info reports after the preamble. CUDA sites should list CUDA_HOME instead of, or as well as, ROCM_PATH.

preamble._comment: A non-interactive SSH session has no `module` command in PATH and no shell profile applied, so the environment must be declared rather than remembered. These entries are rendered into every dispatched command, in this order: modules, then env, then commands. Declare only what the project needs: `module load` is the slowest line here, measured at 1 to 2.5 seconds per command on LUMI, and it is paid every time.
preamble._comment_apply_to_scheduler: Scheduler clients (squeue, sinfo, sacct, sbatch) live in the default PATH at every site we know of, so the preamble is skipped for them — which is most of an assistant's remote calls. Set this to true only if `squeue` on your cluster needs a module first.

file_access._comment: How files are shared between the laptop and the cluster. Only `rsync` is supported: nothing here moves files by itself, so sync-to-remote.sh does it. See LOCAL-MODE.md.

rsync._comment: Applied by sync-to-remote.sh, which is what actually moves files: nothing in hpc-mcp runs rsync, so this list is documentation unless the script reads it. Keep the two in step. Never uses --delete, and a dry run is shown before any transfer.

limits._comment: Bounds the permission model of an agent harness cannot express.
